newsitem.title: UK: European bourses fall, depressed by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: European bourses fall, depressed by Wall St.

text.p: European stocks fell steeply on Friday with investors depressed by overnight selling on Wall Street sparked by jitters over interest rates and a weakening dollar.
On currency markets, the dollar slipped against the mark after stronger-than-expected German economic data on Thursday dampened speculation of a cut in interest rates and boosted the German currency.

London, Frankfurt and Paris, which have all hit peaks in recent weeks. showed big losses within minutes of opening after New York posted a 1.32 percent decline at the close on Thursday. The German and French bourses later clawed back some losses.
"The feeling is that we are very much at the top of the range and the market is going to be volatile," said one dealer in London.
Europe's major bourses, which have largely mirrored the bull run in New York, were rattled after the Dow Jones industrial average ended down 92.75 points at 6,927.38 on Thursday.
Wall Street's weakness came only two days after touching a record of 7,067.46. Investors became nervous about an upturn in long-term interest rates and the weaker dollar.
The currency's recent strength has been an important factor in the stock market's rally. It has drawn considerable investment to U.S. financial markets from outside the country.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, was hardest hit by Wall Street, falling by 0.8 percent by late morning.
"We should have been off more on the Dow," said one derivatives specialist. "Now we're just waiting for the Dow."

But dealers said the market was still underpinned by bid speculation. Shares in Cadbury Schweppes Plc were up 8-1/2p to 493-1/2 on renewed bid speculation, with Unilever Plc seen as a possible predator, dealers said.
Frankfurt, where the computerised IBIS index fell by one percent in pre-bourse deals, later recovered some ground and was showing a loss of only 0.25 percent by late morning.
Floor trade was down by a similar margin on the DAX index, with sentiment hurt by Wall Street and the softer dollar which could harm German exports.
"There seems to be wholesale selling across the board this morning and the big heavyweights, like the chemical companies and Daimler Benz are all down," said one Frankfurt trader.
In Paris, almost every stock in the CAC-40 leading share index turned downwards in early trade but the market regained some poise and was down only a few points by lunch time.

On the currency front, the dollar fell on Thursday's closing levels as expectations diminished of near-term German interest rate cuts and attitudes to the yen turned cautiously more positive, analysts said.

"The bias is towards a firmer mark in the aftermath of yesterday's (German) numbers...running parallel is the more positive yen sentiment that is prevailing in Japan," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered in London.

On the yen side, senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said overnight that foreigners had been buying yen since February 20, and forex rates had been "rather stable" since the G7 meeting of leading industrial countries this month.
The dollar changed little from early morning levels although on a broader canvas the market still prefers the dollar bullish scenario, analysts said.
Currency dealers said there was not much to stir the U.S. currency before Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week., analysts said.
Greenspan is due to speak in Florida at 1340 GMT today, but analysts expected him to save any market-moving comments for his Congressional testimony on Wednesday and Thursday.

Traders spent the morning awaiting the EU's ruling on Italy's controversial euro tax, designed to cut its budget deficit for monetary union. The tax was approved, but that matched expectations and had scant impact on the lira.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6865 marks and 122.75 yen compared to the 1.6895 and 123.07 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 36.4 points at 4,319.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 4.74 points at 2,570.50.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 9.96 points at 3,186.07.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $350.75 an ounce, compared with $346.45 at the London close on Thursday. Silver was at $5.24, up four cents.
